The petition is filed by the petitioner under Sec.166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1989 seeking compensation for an amount of Rs.20,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by him, in a road traffic Riyaz Pasha vs New India Ass Co Ltd on 7 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/13650529/
1 accident.
2.

The brief facts of the petitioner's case are as under:
It is the case of the petitioner that on 01.12.2022 at about 1.45 pm., when the petitioner was travelling in the Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-05-AD- 3371, the driver of the said bus driving the same at high speed in a rash and negligent manner and when the said bus was proceeding at Belluru Bridge, on Kolar - Bengaluru NH - 75 Road,
Narasapura Hobli, Kolar District there was road hump, due to sudden SCCH - 26 3 MVC No.7350/2022 jump from up and down, the petitioner lost control and fell down from the bus and sustained severe injuries to his right leg and head.

Immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to S.N.R.Hospital, Kolar, after first aid treatment, he was taken to NIMHANS Hospital,
Bengaluru then shifted to Sanjay Gandhi Hospital wherein took treatment as an inpatient and undergone operation, closed reduction internal fixation was done.
The Vemagal Police have registered a case against the driver of the Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-05-AD-3371 in Crime No.236/2022.
After investigation, the Police have filed a charge sheet against him for the offence punishable under Section 279, 338 IPC.
At the time of accident, the first respondent was insurer and second respondent was R.C Owner of the Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-05-AD-3371.
Hence, both the respondents are jointly and severally liable for payment of compensation.
After service of summons, the respondent No.2 did not appeared in this petition and he placed exparte.
The Respondent No.1 has appeared through counsel and filed his objection to main petition.
Respondent No.1 - Insurance Company filed its objection that the denying the petition averments.
It has denied the age, avocation and income of the petitioner as he was aged about 21 years, student and doing fruit business and earning Rs.16,000/- per month.

Further contended that, as on the date of accident, the Bus bearing Reg.No.KA- 05-AD-3371 was not having valid RC, FC, permit,
Insurance etc., to ply in place of accident.

Further contended that, as per the records, the petitioner was standing on the foot board and he himself was negligent near the road hump and jumped from the bus without the knowledge of the driver or conductor of the bus, as such the petition is not SCCH - 26 5 MVC No.7350/2022 maintainable for one's own negligence.
It has contended that the owner of the alleged offending vehicle and the concerned police have not complied the mandatory provisions of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act.
It has denied the occurrence and mode of the accident and also involvement of the vehicle.

Further it has contended that, the liability of this respondent, if any is subject to terms and conditions and limitations of policy of insurance issued in favour of the owner and in accordance with the provisions of Motor Vehicles Act, if policy issued.
Hence, the petition is liable to be dismissed against this respondent.
The compensation claimed is highly exorbitant.
For all these reasons, it has prayed for dismissal of the petition.

Whether the Petitioner proves that, he sustained injuries on 01.12.2022 at 01.45 pm., while he was travelling in SCCH - 26 6 MVC No.7350/2022 the Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-05-AD-3371 only due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of the said bus at Bellur Bridge, on Kolar-Bengaluru NH-75 Road, Narasapura Hobli, Kolar District?
2. What compensation the petitioner is entitled for and from whom?
3. What Order or Award?
5. The petitioner in order to prove his case has examined himself as PW.1 and got marked 13 documents as Ex.P1 to Ex.P.13 and during cross through confrontation got marked Ex.D.1.
He has examined his witnesses Dr.Chidanand.K.J.C as PW.2 and got marked three documents as Ex.P.14 to 16.
On the other hand, on behalf of respondent No.1, one witness has examined as RW.1 and got marked four documents as Ex.R.1 to 4 and closed his side evidence.
6. Heard the arguments from both sides.
Perused materials on the entire records.
Learned counsel for petitioner and respondent SCCH - 26 7 MVC No.7350/2022 No.1 has submitted their written arguments.

The learned counsel for petitioner has relied on citation reported in 2011 ACJ 911 (Ravi Vs.
Badrinarayana and Ors.)

It is relevant to note that the respondent No.1 has specifically contended that there is sole negligence of the petitioner who was standing on the foot board and he himself was negligent near the road hump and jumped from the bus without the knowledge of the driver or conductor of the Bus as such the petition is not maintainable for one's own negligence.

Therefore, the burden is on the petitioner to prove that the injuries sustained by him not because of self-fall in the alleged accident but due to the negligence on the part of the driver of alleged Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-05-AD-3371.
10.

Petitioner himself examined as PW.1 and in his evidence has stated that on 01.12.2022 at about SCCH - 26 9 MVC No.7350/2022 1.45 pm., when he was traveling in the Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-05-AD-3371, the driver of the said bus driving the same at high speed in a rash and negligent manner and when the said bus was proceeding at Belluru Bridge, on Kolar - Bengaluru NH - 75 Road, Narasapura Hobli, Kolar District there was road hump, due to sudden jump from up and down, he lost control and fell down from the bus and sustained severe injuries to his right leg and head.

11. PW.1 in support of his version, he has produced the certified copy of FIR, complaint, spot panchanama, seizure panchanama, IMV report, wound certificate and charge sheet at Ex.P.1, 2, 4 to 8.
12.
I have perused Ex.P.1, 2, 4 to 8.

From these documents, it is clear that the accident took place on 01.12.2022 at about 01.45 pm., and the FIR at Ex.P.1 in crime No.0236/2022 came to be SCCH - 26 10 MVC No.7350/2022 registered on 03.12.2022 at around 14.10, at Vemagal Police Station for the offences punishable u/s 279, 337 of IPC and complaint at Ex.P.2 was lodged by father of petitioner on 03.12.2022, Ex.P.3 is the statement of injured, Ex.P.4 - spot panchanama which done on 03.12.2022 at Kolar taluk, Narasapura Hobli, Bellur Bridge, Kolar - Bengaluru NH -75 road wherein it discloses same as in petition.

Further the records reveal that thereafter, the police conducted investigation and filed charge-sheet at Ex.P.8 against the driver of the bus for the offences punishable u/s 279, 338 of IPC.
13.
The learned counsel for the respondent No.1 has cross examined PW-1.
I have perused the entire cross-examination of PW-1, PW.1 denied that the accident occurred due to his own negligence.
The learned counsel for the respondent No.1 has not elicited anything from the mouth of PW-1 to SCCH - 26 11 MVC No.7350/2022 disbelieve his version.
There is nothing on record to show that the charge-sheet filed by the police is defective or collusive.

Moreover, it is settled law that the term "rashness and negligence" has to be construed lightly while deciding a petition for claim of compensation under the MV Act as compare to the word "rashness and negligence" as finds mention Riyaz Pasha vs New India Ass Co Ltd on 7 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/13650529/
4 in the Indian Penal Code.

Therefore, on over all appreciation of evidence, I am of the opinion that the accident occurred due to the negligence of driver of the Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-05-AD-3371 which belongs to the respondent No.2.
However, the charge sheet is also not challenged by the respondents.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 in the affirmative.

14. ISSUE NO.2:
SCCH - 26 12 MVC No.7350/2022 AGE, AVOCATION AND INCOME: PW.1 has produced his Aadhaar card at Ex.P.11.
As per which the date of birth of the petitioner is shown as 19.06.2002.
Therefore, as on the date of accident he was aged about 20 years.

Therefore, the appropriate multiplier for the said age group as per Sarla Verma's case is '18'.
15.
The petitioner has deposed that prior to accident, he was studying at B.Com., and also doing fruit vending business and earning sum of Rs.16,000/- p.m.
Except oral suggestion he has not produced any document to show his avocation and actual income.
Therefore, it is necessary to take into account notional income of the petitioner while calculating the compensation.
As per the guidelines issued by the Hon'ble Karnataka State Legal Service Authority the notional income of the petitioner is taken as Rs.15,500/- as the accident took place in the year 2022.

PW.1 has deposed that after the accident he was taken to S.N.R.Hospital, Kolar after first aid he was taken to NIMHANS and then taken to Sanjay Gandhi Hospital wherein he took treatment as an inpatient for 9 days and undergone open reduction internal fixation surgery and discharged with an advice to take follow up treatment.

He has spent a sum of Rs.75,000/- towards medical expenses,
food and nourishment, attendant charges and for incidental expenses.
Further deposed that, prior to the accident he was hale and healthy, he was studying at B.Com,and also doing fruit vending business and earning a sum of Rs.16,000/- per month.
As per Ex-P7 - wound certificate petitioner sustained tend right ankle abrasion over lateral aspect of right ankle.
X-ray shows bimalleolar fracture of right.
Doctor has opined that the said injury is grievous in nature.

Petitioner has produced his discharge summary marked at Ex.P.9 SCCH - 26 14 MVC No.7350/2022 issued by Sanjay Gandhi Hospital wherein he was admitted as an inpatient from 01.12.2022 to 09.12.2022 i.e.,
for 9 days.
17. The petitioner in order to show his disability has examined Dr.Chidanand.K.J.C as PW.2.

He has filed affidavit for his examination in chief and deposed that a patient by name Riyaz Pasha aged about 20 years old came to their hospital on 01.12.2022 with alleged history of RTA and he sustained injuries like post traumatic right bimalleolar ankle fracture (abrasion over anterior aspect of ankle).
The patient underwent surgery in the form of ORIF with plate and screws and discharged on 09.12.2022.

On 04.01.2024, patient came for disability assessment and noted that, range of movements of ankle restricted, healed scar mark over ankle noted, quadriceps wasting is seen,
associated with pain on movements knee and ankle, daily activities cross leg sitting, squatting for SCCH - 26 15 MVC No.7350/2022 using Indian toilets were found to be difficulty in left limb.

During examination in chief OPD record, case sheet and X-rays were marked at Ex.P.14 to 16 and during cross examination he has deposed that, as per Ex.P.16 - X-ray one injury got united and another one is malunited.
18. It is relevant to note that according to PW.2 has assessed whole body disability at 14%.

It is well settled law that it is the impact of the physical disability on the particular avocation of the petitioner which is relevant for the purpose of assessment of compensation under the head of loss of future income as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Rajkumar's case reported in (2011) 1 SCCH - 26 16 MVC No.7350/2022 SCC 343.
By looking into the record it seems that PW.2 has assessed disability of the Petitioner at higher side.
Therefore, the Petitioner might be having 10% disability to the whole body which cannot be ruled out.
19. PAIN & SUFFERINGS:
On account of the accidental injuries the petitioner has undergone pain and sufferings to some extent.
Thus, this Tribunal awards a sum of Rs.40,000/- under this head.
20. LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID-UP PERIOD:

Considering the age, nature of injuries,
treatment given as inpatient in the hospital and as an outpatient, it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out his avocation normally for at least 2 months.
Thus by taking into account the notional income of the petitioner, this Tribunal awards Rs.31,000/-(15,500/- x 2) under this head.

21. ATTENDANT CHARGES, EXTRA SCCH - 26 17 MVC No.7350/2022 NUTRITIOUS FOOD &
CONVEYANCE CHARGES :
As already stated supra the petitioner took treatment as an inpatient for nearly 9 days as it could be seen from Ex.P.9 and also produced Ex.P.10 - OPD record.

The petitioner has produced Ex.P.12 - medical bills of Rs.13,316/- along with Ex.P.13 - medical prescriptions.

Hence,
Petitioner is awarded 13,316/- towards Medical Expenses.

As on the date of accident he was aged about 20 years.

Therefore, the appropriate multiplier for the said age group as per Sarla Verma's case is '18'.
SCCH - 26 18 MVC No.7350/2022 This Tribunal has already assessed the notional income of the petitioner at Rs.15,500/- p.m.

Hence, a sum of Rs.3,34,800/-
(Rs.15,500 X 12 X 18 X 10/100) is awarded under this head.

sentences.text: Section 82 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1939, states that "No person driving or in charge of a motor vehicle shall carry any person or permit any person to be carried on the running board or otherwise than within the body of the vehicle".
In the case of a bus, conductor is also in charge of the vehicle since it is his duty to admit passengers and issue tickets.
It is the duty of the driver and conductor to see that footboard passengers are not allowed in the bus and to see that bus is not set in motion when there are passengers on the footboard.
Driver may not be in a position to observe if there are passengers on the footboard.
It is the duty of the conductor to give appropriate directions to the driver.

Where the conductor gives signal for the bus to move or the driver starts the bus without waiting for such an instruction, the starting and moving of SCCH - 26 24 MVC No.7350/2022 the bus with passengers on the footboard is a rash and negligent act.
Taking the bus to the extreme left side on a bridge which has pillars is fraught with danger and risk to passengers on the footboard.
It was the duty of the driver to have ensured passage of the bus without any harm to passengers.
If such passage could not be secured, it was his duty to stop the bus to allow the bus from the opposite direction to pass by.
Swerving the bus to the extreme left side of the road on a bridge with pillars on it when there are footboard passengers in the bus, is by itself a rash and negligent act.
Such rash and negligent driving of the bus casts vicarious liability on the owner of the bus in an action for compensation by persons injured in an accident caused by such driving.
The contra-finding of the Tribunal cannot stand.
Further held that The correct principle appears to be what we have already indicated.

It is the duty of the conductor to see that the bus SCCH - 26 25 MVC No.7350/2022 is set in motion only after all alighting passengers have alighted and passengers intending to travel in the bus board the bus.
Boarding a bus does not mean merely entering the footboard.
Boarding the bus means getting inside the bus and either sitting in a seat or standing in the space reserved for standing passengers.
A conductor has a statutory duty to see that there are no footboard passengers.
If a passenger is on the footboard and there is no space at all for him to sit or stand inside the bus, he must be asked to get down and the bus can be set in motion only after he alights.

When there is sitting or standing space inside the bus, it is the duty of the conductor to see that a passenger who is on the footboard gets inside the bus and seats himself or stands in the space reserved for standing passengers before giving signal for the bus to start.
This corresponds with the driver's duty to ensure that bus is moved only after ensuring safe travel conditions.
In the discharge of his duty he is largely guided by the instructions of the SCCH - 26 26 MVC No.7350/2022 conductor.

If a bus with no vacant seat and no standing space is started when a passenger is on the footboard and he is not asked to alight from the bus or not cautioned against travel on footboard and accident takes place and the footboard passenger sustains injury, wholly or partly on account of his position on the footboard, he cannot be held to be guilty of contributory negligence.

It may be that if he refuses to alight in spite of the direction by the conductor or if he is cautioned about the risk he is undertaking by travel on footboard, it is not possible to absolve Riyaz Pasha vs New India Ass Co Ltd on 7 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/13650529/
9 him of the responsibility in the accident.

sentences.text: We, therefore, hold that the claimant was not guilty of contributory negligence.
In view of the citation in (1990) 1 KLT 607, the citations relied by the respondent No.1 is not applicable to this case.

Therefore the contention of the respondents cannot be accepted the accident was occurred on the contributory negligence of the SCCH - 26 27 MVC No.7350/2022 petitioner and there is a contributory negligence.
This court has held that the accident was occurred on the negligence of driver of offending motorcycle.
Therefore the respondent No.1 and 2 being a owner and insurer of the bus are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
However, the respondent No.1 being the insurer of offending motorcycle is liable to pay compensation of Rs. 4,79,116/- with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
Accordingly, I answer the issue No.2 in the partly affirmative.
28. ISSUE NO.3:

For the aforesaid reasons, I proceed to pass the following :-
-: ORDER :-
The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.4,79,116/- (Rupees Four Lakhs seventy nine thousand one SCCH - 26 28 MVC No.7350/2022 hundred sixteen only)
with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
However, the respondent No.1 being insurer of offending Bus is directed to deposit the compensation amount in this tribunal within one month from the date of this order.
The expenses to be incurred for future medication shall not carry any interest.
After deposit of compensation, entire amount shall be released to the petitioner through E-payment upon proper verification.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-
Draw an award accordingly.

opennyai_summary.issue:
Whether the Petitioner proves that, he sustained injuries on 01.12.2022 at 01.45 pm., while he was travelling in SCCH - 26 6 MVC No.7350/2022 the Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-05-AD-3371 only due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of the said bus at Bellur Bridge, on Kolar-Bengaluru NH-75 Road, Narasapura Hobli, Kolar District?

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Therefore, the burden is on the petitioner to prove that the injuries sustained by him not because of self-fall in the alleged accident but due to the negligence on the part of the driver of alleged Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-05-AD-3371.
10.
There is nothing on record to show that the charge-sheet filed by the police is defective or collusive.
Moreover, it is settled law that the term "rashness and negligence" has to be construed lightly while deciding a petition for claim of compensation under the MV Act as compare to the word "rashness and negligence" as finds mention Riyaz Pasha vs New India Ass Co Ltd on 7 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/13650529/
4 in the Indian Penal Code.
This is because the provisions of M.V.Act dealing with compensation are benevolent legislation and not a penal one.
It is well settled law that it is the impact of the physical disability on the particular avocation of the petitioner which is relevant for the purpose of assessment of compensation under the head of loss of future income as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Rajkumar's case reported in (2011) 1 SCCH - 26 16 MVC No.7350/2022 SCC 343.
On perusal of the contents of petition and SCCH - 26 20 MVC No.7350/2022 contents of objection statement as well as oral and documentary evidence, it reveals that, the respondent No.1 is the owner and the respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending bus bearing Registration No. No.KA-05-AD-3371
Therefore the accident was occurred on the contributory negligence of petitioner.
It is the duty of the conductor to give appropriate directions to the driver.
Where the conductor gives signal for the bus to move or the driver starts the bus without waiting for such an instruction, the starting and moving of SCCH - 26 24 MVC No.7350/2022 the bus with passengers on the footboard is a rash and negligent act.
Taking the bus to the extreme left side on a bridge which has pillars is fraught with danger and risk to passengers on the footboard.
It was the duty of the driver to have ensured passage of the bus without any harm to passengers.
If such passage could not be secured, it was his duty to stop the bus to allow the bus from the opposite direction to pass by.
Swerving the bus to the extreme left side of the road on a bridge with pillars on it when there are footboard passengers in the bus, is by itself a rash and negligent act.
Such rash and negligent driving of the bus casts vicarious liability on the owner of the bus in an action for compensation by persons injured in an accident caused by such driving.
It is the duty of the conductor to see that the bus SCCH - 26 25 MVC No.7350/2022 is set in motion only after all alighting passengers have alighted and passengers intending to travel in the bus board the bus.
Boarding a bus does not mean merely entering the footboard.
Boarding the bus means getting inside the bus and either sitting in a seat or standing in the space reserved for standing passengers.
A conductor has a statutory duty to see that there are no footboard passengers.
If a passenger is on the footboard and there is no space at all for him to sit or stand inside the bus, he must be asked to get down and the bus can be set in motion only after he alights.
When there is sitting or standing space inside the bus, it is the duty of the conductor to see that a passenger who is on the footboard gets inside the bus and seats himself or stands in the space reserved for standing passengers before giving signal for the bus to start.
This corresponds with the driver's duty to ensure that bus is moved only after ensuring safe travel conditions.
In the discharge of his duty he is largely guided by the instructions of the SCCH - 26 26 MVC No.7350/2022 conductor.
If a bus with no vacant seat and no standing space is started when a passenger is on the footboard and he is not asked to alight from the bus or not cautioned against travel on footboard and accident takes place and the footboard passenger sustains injury, wholly or partly on account of his position on the footboard, he cannot be held to be guilty of contributory negligence.
It may be that if he refuses to alight in spite of the direction by the conductor or if he is cautioned about the risk he is undertaking by travel on footboard, it is not possible to absolve Riyaz Pasha vs New India Ass Co Ltd on 7 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/13650529/
9 him of the responsibility in the accident.
We, therefore, hold that the claimant was not guilty of contributory negligence.
